about: How an official's term is read by policy area (owner, Nov 8: 'if you're having a good term except for education, then you might get a strike... this needs to work with the entire game'). Each area is a few of the outcome web's own measures with the direction that is better (+1 when more is better, -1 when less is). The read of an area is how far its measures moved since the term began, as a slide between -1 (as bad as the scale) and 1 (as good); nothing flips at a point. It holds no sentence and decides nothing: the director's addresses and the groups' reactions read it.

fullChange.note: The relative change in a measure over a term that reads as most of the way better or worse (a slide of about 0.76 through tanh). Checked against how far the web's measures move over a decade of a played world.

minimumMonths.note: The fewest months of web rows an area is read over; a term shorter than this is not read yet (the web writes one row a month).

answeredBy.about: The bill catalog topics whose questions answer each area of the term read: a hurt address's answer to its worst condition (a governor or mayor), and the question a campaign speaks on when the town's own record went that way. A subject is wider than its area (restoring the vote after a sentence is justice, and no answer to crime; the words lead read it so on Leonidas, Minnesota, Nov 12), so a question answers an area through its catalog topic. TUNABLE wording of the match, checked by reading composed addresses and a campaign's acts in three named places. A budget line ("budget-line:<line>") answers an area when the line bears on it (a line the speaker backs in that area is a response; owner rule via the words lead, Nov 12: a hurt address answers its own bad news), so a mayor, who holds a few policy questions and the town's budget lines, answers pay through welfare and income security, and jobs through regional development.

warmupMonths.note: The months a world's town needs before its records show a trend and not the settling in from the records it opened with. Read from one played year in Algiers, Vermont (seed r7): unemployment ran 0.3 percent to 5.7 percent and poverty 9.6 percent to 18.6 percent across the first twelve months and was still rising in the fourteenth. The warm-up is a stopgap for that drift (SG-WORDS-term-read-warmup): the economy's start is the owner of the fix.

jurisdictionFigures.about: The measures a state's or the country's own monthly records keep, by the web measure they stand for (owner, Nov 14: 'it's all one simulation'). A state reads the country tier's kept months for it (`countryStateMonth`), the real coarse months before the opening included, shifted to meet the tier at the opening; the country reads the macro module's months, real history included, so a term already under way at the opening reads from real months with no warm-up. Household income is what the regions' jobs pay for each resident (jobs times hourly earnings over people); poverty is not kept for a state or the country, so a pay read is the income measure alone and no poverty figure is invented. An area none of its measures appear here for is read the old way, as the mean over the places the web keeps.
